title: Introduce release anchors and profile stability validator
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Context: onboarding churn for model profiles has caused noisy changelogs and fragile downstream rollout decisions. Recent incidents showed multiple small profile edits (formatting/ordering) surfaced as breaking deltas which forced manual triage. Goal: add a lightweight, forward-compatible mechanism to mark canonical releases ("release anchors") in model metadata and a profile stability validator that demotes noise (ordering/rounding) and flags actionable regressions. This PR introduces a v2 onboarding metadata migration, a release_anchor field, a stability-check gaiter that runs as part of the onboard pipeline, and an update to the changelog assembler so release notes are generated per-anchor rather than per-upload.

What this changes: 1) metadata schema v2: optional "release_anchor" (string) plus a small semantic version stamp for profile artifacts; 2) profile stability validator: rule-set that normalizes non-semantic diffs (ordering, whitespace, float rounding) and runs model-profile evaluation heuristics (latency median, perplexity delta, embedding-cosine drift) to produce a stability_score; 3) changelog generator updates: groups deltas by release_anchor and collapses low-impact edits into a single "maintenance" bullet when stability_score > 0.95; 4) migration script: migrate_existing_profiles_v2.py to backfill anchors using best-effort (latest stable tag if present, otherwise upload id); 5) pipeline integration: validator integrated into onboard CI job with allow/deny thresholds and suggested mitigation notes.

Checklist: [x] design doc reviewed by ML infra and runtime teams; [x] migration with dry-run mode; [x] unit + integration tests for validator; [x] changelog grouping tests; [x] docs + SDK examples updated; [x] manual smoke test with 3 public models.

Testing notes: validator tested against synthetic diffs and against the existing profile corpus (n=3.2k) in staging; migration dry-run caught ~120 ambiguous anchors which were flagged to the owner mapping table for manual review. CI: unit-tests + onboard-integration + changelog-render passed in sequence. Rollout plan: merge to main, run migration with --dry-run for 48h, then backfill anchors incrementally by namespace during a maintenance window. Backwards compatibility: release_anchor is optional; changelog assembler falls back to current behavior when absent. Security/permissions: migration only reads metadata and writes annotations with the onboard service account; all writes are audited.

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: Can the validator be toggled per-namespace? We need to avoid blocking enterprise uploads with custom profile fields.
Sofia Martinez: Yes — validator is namespace-aware; thresholds live in namespace config and default to non-blocking warns for first 30 days.
Nina Patel: Migration backfill needs to avoid rate spikes against the registry API. How are you batching?
Sofia Martinez: backfill uses a rate-limited worker with exponential backoff and a checkpoint file; default concurrency is 5 per region and configurable.
Rahul Desai: The stability_score thresholds seem conservative — can we provide a suggested remediation path in the changelog when a delta is flagged?
Sofia Martinez: Added suggested remediation strings for common regression classes (quantization mismatch, tokenizer updates, seed drift) and a link to the onboarding troubleshooting doc.
Liam O'Connor: Approving after CI green and docs update.
Nina Patel: Approving — tested the staging backfill and sanity checked release-note grouping.
Merge Bot: merged commit d5b2f09 into main via squash
release_notes:
- Add optional release_anchor metadata to model profiles to mark canonical releases.
- Add profile stability validator to reduce noisy changelog deltas (normalizes ordering/whitespace/float rounding).
- Changelog assembler now groups changes by release_anchor and collapses maintenance edits.
- Migration tool to backfill v2 metadata with dry-run safety and rate-limited backfill.
notes: This PR focuses on reducing operator noise and improving signal for release notes; it intentionally keeps release_anchor optional to maintain backward compatibility. The validator is designed to be conservative by default and tuned via namespace config.
smoke_test_summary: Staging run against 3 public models produced expected grouped changelogs; migration dry-run flagged 120 ambiguous anchors for manual reconciliation; no blocker regressions observed.
post_merge_actions: 1) Run migrate_to_v2.py --dry-run across all namespaces for 48h; 2) Review flagged ambiguous anchors and update mapping; 3) Switch follow-up runs to --apply per-namespace during scheduled windows; 4) Monitor changelog drift and file a follow-up ENG ticket if >0.5% of profiles generate high-impact flags.
rollback_plan: Disable anchor-based grouping via feature flag and revert change in changelog assembler; migration is non-destructive by default in dry-run mode.
